newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks tumble lower in early trade.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks tumble lower in early trade.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks tumbled lower on Thursday morning, due chiefly to negative sentiment in the futures market and a concentration of buying interest on newcomer Beijing Enterprises, brokers said.
"This is the stock of the future," said David Williamson, director at Indosuez W.I. Carr. "I am telling all my clients to buy it."
The Hang Seng Index was trading 99 points lower at 14,456 after 40 minutes of trade, off the morning low of 14,435.53, on heavy volume of more than HK$3.0 billion.
"In the short to medium term, we may have seen a top in the market," said a futures trader with a U.S. brokerage. "Today's close will give us a better indication."
The May Hang Seng Index futures contract which expires later on Thursday, was trading 90 points lower at 14,465 and the June contract was 80 points lower at 14,525.
"With the expiry of futures we will probably be up and down 50 points and could close slightly down on the day," said a broker with a large UK house.
"There are still quite a few long positions out there."
Properties and utility shares led the market down. Mid cap issues were also weak.
Sun Hung Kai Properties lost HK$1.50 to HK$93.25.
Hongkong Telecommunications Ltd, which had been the focus of recent short-term trading, was HK$0.20 lower at HK$16.80. HSBC Holdings Plc was HK$1.00 lower at HK$228.00.
China Resources slipped HK$0.90 to HK$26.55 on moderate trade of HK$90 million.
Red chip newcomer Beijing Enterprises Holdings debuted at HK$41.00, hit a high of HK$45.00, then eased to HK$41.50.
Turnover in the share was a rose to more than HK$1.35 billion in the first hour of trade.
